In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of selective translation regulation of chloroplast proteins in response to light and dark.
the mechanism of light-regulated gene expression in chloroplasts.
the mechanism by which the synthesis of chlorophyll apoproteins of photosynthetic reaction centers is regulated in response to illumination of etiolated seedlings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
light regulates translation of the chloroplast proteins by affecting both the elongation and initiation of polypeptide synthesis.
illumination of dark-grown seedlings results in a general stimulation of translation in chloroplasts, but that this stimulation is not uniform for all chloroplast mRNAs.
the selective activation of psaA, psaB and psbA translation observed in the present study is the result of a light-induced increase in the translational activity of the plastid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
light regulates the synthesis of the chloroplast-encoded proteins of Photosystem I by controlling the elongation of polypeptide chains on polysomes.
the selective activation of translation elongation of psaA/psaB transcripts is accompanied by a stimulation of translation initiation of all chloroplast transcripts.
illumination causes a general stimulation of translation initiation and a selective activation of translation elongation of chlorophyll apoproteins of PS I.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chloroplast translation system is very complex, and it is not sufficient to simply measure the abundance of mRNA to predict the abundance of protein.
light regulates translation in chloroplasts in two ways: (i) it stimulates translation initiation, and (ii) it activates translation elongation of specific mRNAs.
the chloroplast is an active site of protein translation in the dark.
